# Verify native library loading and the exact symbols a Dart wrapper uses

## Platform difference

A Dart FFI wrapper can compile while its OH shared library is missing, loaded from the wrong location or missing a lazily resolved symbol.

## Implementation

MR builds the shared QuickJS/native core for OH and selects libquickjs_c_bridge.so explicitly. Pica Comic expands loader candidates, adds process-symbol fallback and diagnostics. Simple Live removes a positive memoryLimit argument because its selected library lacks jsSetMemoryLimit, whose lookup is otherwise lazy. NipaPlay adds OH loaders and a QuickJS adapter rather than assuming the desktop loader works.

## Applicability

Validate each exact library/ABI/wrapper combination. A process-symbol fallback only helps when the expected symbol is actually exported in that process.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

Simple Live's workaround avoids the unresolved-symbol path but also removes that resource bound; it does not demonstrate equivalent limits elsewhere. Bundled arm64 libraries do not establish other architecture support.

## Verification

Inspect symbol tables and packaged paths; execute optional wrapper operations that trigger lazy lookup, invalid inputs and resource exhaustion scenarios appropriate to the engine.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
